name: Point-Based Ray Tracing for Visibility
definition: A sparse visibility oracle that evaluates transmittance along sampled light directions using a BVH of Gaussian proxies, allowing evaluation from any point in space in any direction, unlike the camera-tied rasterizer.
summary: Point-Based Ray Tracing for Visibility is a sparse oracle that evaluates transmittance along arbitrary rays using Gaussian proxies and a BVH, decoupling visibility from screen-space projection to enable consistent blending with standard 3D Gaussian Splatting.
